texts.preamble: Vijay Dairy & Farm Products (P) Ltd vs The District Revenue Officer on 3 September, 2018 Author: V.Parthiban Bench: V.Parthiban Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 03.09.2018 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice V.Parthiban W.P.(Md) No.353 of 2018 and W.M.P.(MD)Nos.368 and 369 of 2018 Vijay Dairy & Farm Products (P) Ltd., represented by its Managing Director, J.Madam Mohan. ... Petitioner vs. 1.The District Revenue Officer, cum Additional District Magistrate, Karur. 2.The Designated Officer, Tamilnadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Karur District, Karur. ... Respondents Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of writ of Certiorari to call for the records to the order of the first respondent, dated 28.07.2014 made in Na.Ka.No.K2/10812/2014 and quash the same. !For Petitioner : Mr.V.Sitharanjandas ^For Respondents : Mr.B.Pugalendhi Additional Advocate General assisted by Vijay Dairy & Farm Products (P) Ltd vs The District Revenue Officer on 3 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151992993/ 1 Mr.A.Muthukaruppan Additional Government Pleader :Order
texts.facts: The writ petition is filed against the order passed by the first respondent, dated 28.07.2014, under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. This writ petition was entertained and an interim order was passed by this Court on the ground that the appellate Tribunal as envisaged in the Act was not established.
texts.arguments: 4. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has the benefit of interim order passed by this Court during the pendency of the writ petition and therefore, the petitioner may be given interim protection till the appeal is taken up for hearing by the appellate Tribunal. 5. Considering the submission made by the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, this Court directs that the impugned order shall not be given effect to by the respondents till the appeal is taken up for hearing by the appellate Tribunal.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 4. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has the benefit of interim order passed by this Court during the pendency of the writ petition and therefore, the petitioner may be given interim protection till the appeal is taken up for hearing by the appellate Tribunal.
texts.respondent_arguments: 5. Considering the submission made by the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, this Court directs that the impugned order shall not be given effect to by the respondents till the appeal is taken up for hearing by the appellate Tribunal.
